destinations.name: Sissu / Atal Tunnel
destinations.safety: Atal Tunnel is usually kept open. After fresh snow, police sometimes let only 4×4 cars with chains go beyond Solang towards the Rohtang/Sissu side. Carry chains in a 2WD SUV and fill fuel in Manali. Check Manali traffic police the night before.

destinations.snow_months: Typically November to March; some years it starts in late October.

destinations.name: Solang Valley
destinations.safety: The Manali–Solang road is usually fine for a 2WD SUV when it is clear and ploughed. After fresh snow it can close or become chains-only. Weekends are very crowded. Do not drive onto ski slopes or packed-snow side tracks.

destinations.name: Narkanda
destinations.safety: The NH5 town road is usually kept open. The spur to Hatu Peak is steeper and ices over; a 2WD SUV may need chains after snow, or you can skip Hatu and stay in town. Fill fuel before the last climb.
destinations.snow_months: Typically December to February. More reliable than Kufri, less than Kinnaur or Lahaul.

destinations.name: Kufri
destinations.safety: Roads are busy and can be icy. A 2WD SUV is usually fine to the main market when the road is clear. Parking is tight. Do not follow ponies or crowd vehicles onto snow banks.

destinations.snow_months: Typically December to February, but snow here is less reliable than at higher places on this list.

destinations.name: Chitkul
destinations.safety: Long drive: NH5 into the Sangla valley road, which is narrow with drop-offs. Last reliable petrol is usually around Reckong Peo or Bhabanagar — fill up. After heavy snow the valley road can close. A 2WD SUV is commonly used when the road is clear and ploughed. Do not push through fresh unploughed snow. There is little help after Karcham at night.

photos.author: Manojkhurana

destinations.snow_months: Typically November to March. The village is high, so it can get snow earlier than Sangla.

destinations.name: Sangla
destinations.safety: Same valley road as Chitkul, a little lower and busier. Fill petrol at Reckong Peo or Bhabanagar. A 2WD SUV is usually fine when the road is ploughed. Do not drive the last Chitkul stretch after a fresh, unploughed fall.

destinations.name: Kalpa
destinations.safety: Kalpa sits on a steep spur above Reckong Peo, off NH5. The village road can be icy. A 2WD SUV is usually fine when it is clear. Fill fuel in Reckong Peo. After heavy snow, walk the last icy lanes rather than forcing the car.

photos.author: Amanpanta1990

destinations.name: Rakchham
destinations.safety: Sits on the Sangla–Chitkul road. Same fuel and closure advice as Chitkul. A quiet base if Chitkul rooms are full or the last stretch is in poor shape. 2WD is usually fine when the road is ploughed.

photos.title: Himalayan view from Rakchham village, Kinnaur, Himachal Pradesh, India- 2014-02-15 12-20.jpg
photos.author: User:Traveller arunava

destinations.name: Jalori Pass / Jibhi
destinations.safety: In winter, drive to Jibhi via Aut and Banjar. Do not plan to cross Jalori Pass after snowfall — it is often shut. A 2WD SUV is usually fine to Jibhi when the Banjar road is open. Carry chains only if you go up towards Shoja or the pass, and turn back if the road is not ploughed.
destinations.snow_months: The pass (about 3,140 m) often holds snow from December to March and is often closed then. Jibhi village is much lower (about 1,780 m) and gets less snow.

destinations.name: Chanshal / Dodra Kwar
destinations.safety: This is the highest road on the list. A 2WD SUV should not attempt Chanshal Pass with fresh or packed snow. Go only when Rohru locals and the local administration say the pass is open and ploughed or dry. There is almost no recovery once you are on the top. Dodra Kwar is a further 36 km after the pass.
destinations.snow_months: The pass (about 3,760 m) can hold snow from November into spring, and is often closed for a long mid-winter stretch. Dodra Kwar, beyond the pass, can be cut off.

destinations.name: Auli
destinations.safety: Drive to Joshimath, then either the Auli road or the ropeway. After snow, the Auli road may need chains or may close; the ropeway is the safer way up if it is running. Check the Joshimath road status the night before. Fill fuel in Joshimath. A 2WD SUV is usually fine to Joshimath when that highway is open.
destinations.snow_months: Typically December to March (it is a ski meadow).

destinations.name: Harsil
destinations.safety: Beyond Uttarkashi on the Gangotri road, along the Bhagirathi river. The road can close after heavy snow or landslides. A 2WD SUV is usually fine when the road is open and ploughed. Fill fuel in Uttarkashi. There may be checkpoints.  the valley and riverside villages, not a temple run.

destinations.name: Chakrata
destinations.safety: Forest roads can be narrow and foggy. A 2WD SUV is usually fine in clear weather. After a rare snow, roads ice over. The Tiger Falls spur is a side road — go in daylight. Fill fuel in Dehradun or Vikasnagar.
destinations.snow_months: Typically December to February, and not every year — it is the lowest ‘snow’ town on the main list, so treat snow as a bonus, not a promise.

destinations.name: Manali
destinations.safety: Main town road stays open most of winter. Old Manali and hotel lanes get icy after snow. Traffic jams are common on weekends near the Mall and towards Solang.

destinations.name: Sethan
destinations.safety: Small village above Prini on a narrow, steep road. After snow the last stretch is often walk-only. Leave the car lower if locals advise it.

destinations.name: Shimla
destinations.safety: Snow comes only a few times a winter. Roads ice over in the morning and parking is tight. Use town parking and walk the Mall.

photos.title: A view from Shimlas upper ridge looking north to the snow-capped Himalaya.jpg
photos.author: Liz Highleyman from San Francisco, USA

destinations.name: Dalhousie
destinations.safety: Hill roads from Banikhet are usually open. Snow days make the inner roads icy; drive slowly and avoid shaded bends early morning.

destinations.name: Khajjiar
destinations.safety: The Dalhousie–Khajjiar road runs through forest and can close or turn icy after a heavy fall. Go mid-day and check with Dalhousie locals.

destinations.name: McLeod Ganj
destinations.safety: Town itself rarely gets heavy snow; snow is usually up at Triund (trek). Roads are steep and narrow with heavy traffic.

destinations.name: Shoja
destinations.safety: Above Jibhi on the Jalori road. Steep and narrow; after snow it is often chains-only or closed above Shoja. Do not attempt Jalori Pass after fresh snow.

destinations.name: Keylong
destinations.safety: Reached through Atal Tunnel. In deep winter, roads beyond Sissu may be restricted after snowfall; police often allow only 4x4 with chains. Check Lahaul police updates.

destinations.name: Kaza (Spiti)
destinations.safety: In winter Spiti is reached only via Shimla–Kinnaur (Kunzum route is closed). Very cold, remote, landslide and black-ice prone. Experienced drivers only; carry chains and extra fuel.

destinations.name: Chopta
destinations.safety: After heavy snow the road from Ukhimath/Duggalbitta to Chopta often closes and you may need to walk. Fill fuel in Ukhimath or earlier.

photos.author: Alok

destinations.name: Munsiyari
destinations.safety: Very long mountain drive via Thal or Birthi. Kalamuni top can get snow and close briefly. Drive in daylight only.

destinations.name: Dhanaulti
destinations.safety: Short drive from Mussoorie. Gets busy and jams on snow days. Roads ice up in shaded forest stretches.

destinations.name: Mussoorie
destinations.safety: Snow is occasional. Massive weekend traffic; park and walk. Morning ice on the Kempty and Landour roads.

destinations.name: Sankri
destinations.safety: Base village for the Kedarkantha trek. Narrow road beyond Mori/Naitwar; after heavy snow vehicles may stop below Sankri.

destinations.name: Raithal
destinations.safety: Village road off the Gangotri highway above Bhatwari. Steep last stretch that can ice over. Snow fields are a trek above the village.

destinations.name: Mukteshwar
destinations.safety: Snow comes a few times a winter. Narrow hill roads; drive slowly on shaded bends.

destinations.name: Gulmarg
destinations.safety: Tangmarg–Gulmarg road is kept open but chains are often mandatory after snow, and police may stop non-local cars. Check J&K traffic advisories.

destinations.name: Sonamarg
destinations.safety: Srinagar–Sonamarg road (with Z-Morh tunnel) is mostly open, but avalanche-prone stretches close after heavy snow. Do not go beyond Sonamarg towards Zojila in winter.

destinations.name: Pahalgam
destinations.safety: Main road from Anantnag stays open. Side valleys (Aru, Chandanwari, Betaab) may close in deep snow.

destinations.name: Doodhpathri
destinations.safety: Meadow road from Khansahib can close in heavy snow. Limited facilities; go as a day trip from Srinagar.

photos.title: A bench with scenic view Doodhpathri southwest Jammu Kashmir India.jpg
photos.author: Ankur P from Pune, India

destinations.name: Yusmarg
destinations.safety: Quiet meadow with a single road that may be restricted after snowfall. Limited stays.

destinations.name: Patnitop
destinations.safety: Old NH44 road up from Kud/Batote. Chenani–Nashri tunnel bypasses it, so take the old road. Gets icy and busy after snow.

destinations.name: Natha Top
destinations.safety: A few km above Patnitop. Often closed or chains-only right after snow; walk if the road is not cleared.

destinations.name: Gurez
destinations.safety: Razdan Pass usually closes for winter after heavy snow (often Dec–Apr). Close to the LoC; registration may be needed. Check before planning.

destinations.name: Lachung
destinations.safety: North Sikkim needs a Protected Area Permit arranged through a registered operator, and outside self-drive cars are usually not allowed beyond Gangtok — you hire a local permit taxi. Landslides are common.

destinations.name: Yumthang Valley
destinations.safety: Day trip from Lachung by local permit taxi. Road may close after heavy snow. Permit rules as for Lachung.

destinations.name: Zero Point (Yumesamdong)
destinations.safety: Very high (about 4,700 m). Altitude sickness risk; go only by local permit taxi, limit time at the top. Often closed after fresh snow.

destinations.name: Lachen
destinations.safety: Same permit rules as Lachung. Base for Gurudongmar Lake. Roads are landslide-prone; follow operator and army advice.

destinations.name: Tsomgo (Changu) Lake
destinations.safety: Permit needed (arranged via registered operators from Gangtok). Road can close after snowfall. Nathu La beyond has extra permit rules for Indian nationals only.

destinations.name: Zuluk
destinations.safety: Old Silk Route with famous zig-zag bends. Permit from Rongli needed. Very icy above Zuluk (Thambi view point, Nathang) in winter.
